metadata.title: Proof Discovery Language
metadata.thesis: PDL is a language for discovery programmes rather than only arguments of correctness. It treats coherence, conceptual nexus, material inference, obstruction, and governed recursion as first-class logical objects, and it distinguishes structural notation from the operations that materially transform one epistemic state into another.

design_principles: Treat bridge objects as typed inferential interfaces.
Make negative and impossibility reasoning first-class.
Make the underlying material-inference operators explicit rather than hiding them in prose.
Embed persistence, aggregation, and loops into the logic itself.

notation_layers.title: Structural Layer
notation_layers.role: Names the epistemic objects under search: anchors, targets, tensions, nexuses, bridge objects, obstructions, programmes, debt, and gates.
notation_layers.binding: This layer says what kind of thing is currently in play.

notation_layers.title: Material-Inference Layer
notation_layers.role: Names the operations that transform one epistemic object into another by licensed, non-monotonic, theorem-grounded moves.
notation_layers.binding: This layer says what inferential move is being performed underneath the structural notation.

notation_layers.title: Governance Layer
notation_layers.role: Names persistence, aggregation, revision, continuation, and stop-control over discovery programmes.
notation_layers.binding: This layer says how the process keeps state, loops, and changes direction without losing epistemic discipline.

primitives.title: Anchor
primitives.role: Grounded theorem body, definition, axiom, or imported result that licenses later moves.
primitives.binding: Material inference starts from anchors, not from topic labels.

primitives.title: Target
primitives.role: The smallest nontrivial payoff or consequence worth organizing the search around.
primitives.binding: Discovery is guided by consequence pressure rather than free exploration.
primitives.platform_binding: Route target claims and queued conjectures.

primitives.title: Tension
primitives.role: A typed gap showing why anchors do not yet reach the target: model mismatch, invariant weakness, transport loss, or barrier pressure.
primitives.binding: Tension is the primitive of discovery, because it identifies where reasoning must change form.
primitives.platform_binding: Statement deltas, obstruction classes, and failure diagnoses.

primitives.title: Conceptual Nexus
primitives.role: A coherent local cluster of anchors, tensions, bridge objects, and barriers that can be reasoned over together.
primitives.binding: Discovery first asks whether there is a coherent nexus before demanding correctness-style closure.
primitives.platform_binding: Bridge portfolios, conceptual dynamics, and discovery branches.

primitives.title: Bridge Object
primitives.role: A witness, invariant, certificate, transport law, normal form, or surrogate problem that could make the target reachable.
primitives.binding: Bridge objects express the conceptual breakthrough required by the search.
primitives.platform_binding: Bridge plans, abstraction conjectures, and candidate carriers.

primitives.title: Obstruction
primitives.role: A barrier, counterexample pattern, impossibility theorem, or non-realization diagnosis that blocks a route.
primitives.binding: Negative mathematics is first-class discovery content, not only a failed proof attempt.
primitives.platform_binding: Blocked results, negative programs, and obstruction maps.

primitives.title: Discovery Program
primitives.role: A paired positive/negative route over a nexus, together with proof debt, decision criteria, and revision triggers.
primitives.binding: A discovery program is the unit of guided scientific work, not an isolated proposition.
primitives.platform_binding: Proof sketches, queue entries, and branch dossiers.

primitives.title: Proof Debt
primitives.role: The set of missing lemmas, unrealized carriers, transport laws, and closure obligations still required for completion.
primitives.binding: Debt is what makes discovery governable instead of open-ended.
primitives.platform_binding: Macro-strategy reports, proof obligations, and critique findings.

primitives.title: Decision Gate
primitives.role: A criterion for continue, revise, import prior art, split regimes, or stop.
primitives.binding: Scientific discovery requires explicit transition rules, not only local generation.
primitives.platform_binding: Work loop, web-search gate, high-reward watch, and meta triggers.

material_inference_operations.title: Extract
material_inference_operations.role: Read a theorem body, definition, or axiom as a usable local commitment rather than as raw text.
material_inference_operations.effect: Turns a grounded anchor into claim-bearing content.
material_inference_operations.platform_binding: Phase 0 normalization, statement excerpts, theorem-body normalizer

material_inference_operations.title: Focus
material_inference_operations.role: Localize the exact tension between grounded anchors and the intended target.
material_inference_operations.effect: Turns diffuse mismatch into a typed tension object.
material_inference_operations.platform_binding: statement deltas, failure diagnoses, obstruction classes

material_inference_operations.title: Concretize
material_inference_operations.role: Turn a coherent conceptual nexus into a candidate bridge object, interface, or surrogate problem.
material_inference_operations.effect: Moves from coherence pressure to an inspectable candidate object.
material_inference_operations.platform_binding: abstraction conjectures, expert conjectures, branch-to-definition outputs

material_inference_operations.title: Transport
material_inference_operations.role: Move an invariant, witness condition, or theorem payload across a regime shift, representation change, or equivalence.
material_inference_operations.effect: Makes cross-model or cross-language claims explicit and testable.
material_inference_operations.platform_binding: transport lemmas, alignment work, HoTT/coherence routes

material_inference_operations.title: Factor
material_inference_operations.role: Split one overloaded route into smaller theorem-sized interfaces or intermediate programmes.
material_inference_operations.effect: Exposes hidden composition and missing middle objects.
material_inference_operations.platform_binding: route decomposition, macro-strategy repair, categorical reframing

material_inference_operations.title: Compose
material_inference_operations.role: Assemble several partial bridges, lemmas, or regime results into one route.
material_inference_operations.effect: Promotes local inferential fragments into an end-to-end programme.

material_inference_operations.title: Obstruct
material_inference_operations.role: Derive the barrier, counterexample pattern, incoherence, or non-realization result that blocks a bridge.
material_inference_operations.effect: Turns failed progress into explicit negative mathematics.
material_inference_operations.platform_binding: negative routes, blocked local theorems, contradiction-first probes

material_inference_operations.title: Revise
material_inference_operations.role: Update a discovery programme after an obstruction, failed proof step, or new prior-art import.
material_inference_operations.effect: Makes conceptual change itself explicit rather than leaving it as narrative drift.
material_inference_operations.platform_binding: revision loops, branch regeneration, meta-guided restarts

material_inference_operations.title: Aggregate
material_inference_operations.role: Combine many local results, failed routes, or branch outcomes into a single higher-order nexus or search diagnosis.
material_inference_operations.effect: Produces a global picture rather than isolated route state.
material_inference_operations.platform_binding: branch synthesis, breakthrough profiles, plausibility aggregation

material_inference_operations.title: Persist
material_inference_operations.role: Turn a proved, disproved, blocked, or imported result into durable problem memory.
material_inference_operations.effect: Stops the system from rediscovering the same local mathematics repeatedly.
material_inference_operations.platform_binding: InformalMathLib persistence, queue state, produced papers, prior-art imports

material_inference_operations.title: Route
material_inference_operations.role: Send a discovery programme to prove, further discovery, prior-art search, or stop.
material_inference_operations.effect: Connects local reasoning to governance decisions.
material_inference_operations.platform_binding: work loop, meta triggers, high-reward continuation, queue promotion

relations.meaning: An anchor licenses a claim or program component.
Items form a stable conceptual nexus under the current representation.
A bridge object makes a route from anchor side to target side materially available.
An invariant survives a transport or re-encoding step.
A barrier or impossibility pattern blocks a route or object.
A representation shift or decomposition changes the search unit.
Several partial bridges or programmes combine into one route.
A discovery result becomes durable memory.
The process re-enters discovery/prove under governed recursion.

judgments.meaning: The KB plus InformalMathLib licenses anchor A as a grounded theorem-body object.
Anchors and tensions form a coherent conceptual nexus worth exploring.
The nexus suggests a bridge object B as the best conceptual move.
Bridge object B preserves invariant I across the intended route.
If realized, bridge object B materially supports the target consequence T.
Bridge object B is blocked or sharpened by obstruction O.
A coherent nexus and bridge object together induce a discovery program P.
A discovery program exposes its proof debt explicitly.
A negative route yields a theorem-shaped impossibility or non-realization claim.
A decision gate routes the programme into prove, revision, prior-art import, or stop.

operational_judgments.meaning: Materially focus the mismatch between anchors and target into an explicit tension X.
Stabilize anchors and tensions into a coherent conceptual nexus N.
Concretize the nexus into a bridge object, map, witness family, or surrogate problem B.
Transport invariant I through bridge B from source regime s to target regime t.
Factor a route r into smaller theorem-sized route fragments.
Derive an obstruction O from the current bridge or route proposal.
Revise programme P into a new programme P' after a negative result or barrier localization.
Aggregate many local route outcomes into a higher-order nexus or diagnosis N*.
Persist result R into durable memory object M.

coordination_principles.title: Coherence Before Closure
coordination_principles.detail: A route is first judged as a coherent nexus of anchors, tensions, and bridge commitments before it is judged as correct.

coordination_principles.title: Positive/Negative Symmetry
coordination_principles.detail: Every discovery program carries both a constructive route and a negative/impossibility route, each capable of yielding mathematical value.

coordination_principles.title: Material Inference First
coordination_principles.detail: Inference moves are justified by theorem bodies, model regimes, barriers, and transport obligations before any correctness-style closure is attempted.

coordination_principles.title: Persistent Scientific Memory
coordination_principles.detail: Queues, InformalMathLib, logs, and branch states are part of the logic itself because discovery depends on not forgetting failed and partial routes.

coordination_principles.title: Governed Recursion
coordination_principles.detail: Loops are legitimate only when proof debt, obstruction pressure, or high-value subresults justify another cycle.

control_objects.title: InformalMathLib
control_objects.role: Persistent theorem memory and imported prior art.

control_objects.title: Proof Queue
control_objects.role: Theorem-shaped frontier for proof or disproof.

control_objects.title: Meta Reflection
control_objects.role: Interpretive layer over what changed in understanding.

well_formed_program_requirements: At least one grounded anchor and one explicit target.
A typed tension explaining why the route is not immediate.
A coherent nexus rather than a bag of related statements.
A positive route, a negative route, and explicit proof debt.
A decision gate specifying continue, revise, import, split, or stop.

example_program.tension: X1: transport from source regime to target regime loses the intended invariant
example_program.bridge: B1 := witness family preserving the source-side hardness profile
operations: ext(A1 => c1): extract the usable lower-bound content from the source theorem body
foc(A1, T1 => X1): isolate the exact transport loss between source and target
conc(N1 => B1): propose the witness family as the bridge object demanded by the nexus
tr_I(B1, source ~> target): test whether the invariant survives the intended transport
obs(B1 => O1): derive the non-realization barrier if the witness family collapses
rev(P1, O1 => P2): revise the route into a transport-obstruction programme
mem(O1 => M1): persist the blocked result into InformalMathLib as negative local theorem memory
example_program.positive_route: If B1 is realizable and preserves the invariant, reduce target T to one route lemma L
example_program.negative_route: If every realization of B1 collapses into the barrier, derive impossibility(B1 -> T)
example_program.decision_gate: If L1 sharpens but L2 fails under barrier A3, reframe as transport-obstruction rather than continue constructive forcing
